outcome: symptoms associated with adenoma size increase during pregnancy (nausea-vomiting, visual impairment)
cohort: The study included 30 patients diagnosed with Non-functioning pituitary adenomas (NFPAs) and without hormone deficiency or excess, accounting for 92 pregnancies in total.
finding: NFPAs, including macroadenomatous NFPAs, were not associated with negative effects on pregnancy outcomes, fetal development, or lactation, nor an increased risk of pregnancy-related complications.
mod_finding: NFPAs were not associated with an increased cesarean section rate.
gest_age: Measured as an outcome (pregnancy week at delivery).
